ai.summary: The Federal Reserve’s latest financial-stability survey found that 87% of surveyed market contacts named AI as a salient risk, up from 50% in May. Respondents cited cyberattacks, complex financing and the risk of an AI-driven market correction.
ai.title: Federal Reserve survey puts AI at the top of financial-stability concerns

ai.summary: A petition seeking Nvidia board action to reinstate Jensen Huang reportedly passed 115,000 signatures, including current and former employees and shareholders. The episode reflects concerns about leadership uncertainty at a company central to AI chip supply.
ai.title: More than 115,000 people sign petition asking Nvidia to reinstate Huang

ai.source: The Decoder, via The Model Beat
ai.summary: Meituan released LongCat-2.5, an agent model with 1.6 trillion total parameters, and says it was trained without Nvidia GPUs. Its release highlights efforts to develop large AI systems using alternative compute hardware.
ai.title: Meituan releases a 1.6-trillion-parameter agent model without Nvidia GPUs

ai.summary: Runway released Praxis-1’s model weights and inference and training code under the Apache 2.0 license. The roughly 27-billion-parameter model is designed to translate visual input and instructions into robot actions.
ai.title: Runway releases Praxis-1 robot-control model under Apache 2.0

quantum.summary: A newly reported cryogenic RF multiplexer combines superconducting-qubit control, readout and flux biasing at millikelvin temperatures with picowatt power consumption. The work addresses a key engineering challenge in scaling control hardware.
quantum.title: CryoCMOS RF multiplexer for superconducting qubit control, readout and flux biasing at millikelvin temperatures with picowatt power consumption

quantum.summary: Atom Computing finalized an agreement with the U.S. Department of Commerce worth up to $100 million for R&D on fault-tolerant, utility-scale quantum systems. The funding is intended to support technology development and expanded testing infrastructure.
quantum.title: Atom Computing signs up to $100M U.S. Department of Commerce contract to support tens-of-thousands-qubit development

quantum.summary: RIKEN researchers reported a simulated method that reduces physical-qubit and gate requirements for preparing states in a quantum error-correcting code, while maintaining similar simulated logical-operation error rates. The result is a circuit-design study, not a hardware demonstration.
quantum.title: RIKEN proposes fewer steps to prepare protected quantum bits

quantum.summary: Researchers from École Normale Supérieure and Google Quantum AI reported a superconducting qubit design that suppresses sensitivity to dielectric loss through parity symmetry. Their measurements indicate that dielectric loss would limit the qubit lifetime to above 10 milliseconds, with flux noise remaining a constraint.
quantum.title: Qubit parity symmetry protects against dielectric loss
